input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual, the indirect/consequential exclusion is mutual, and the Excluded Claims list (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) is uncapped. But the cap basis fails even the fallback: "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as the Implementation Fee only, i.e. the one-time USD 12,000 charge stated in the first Order Form (§ 1.6), and the cap is further confined to that first Order Form. That is an illusory cap well below six months' fees, which is walk-away territory. The same narrow defined term also undercut the § 21.3 payment carve-out. We therefore reset the basis to the greater of the fees paid or payable under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, and confirmed that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap; all other Section 21 wording, including the "undisputed"/"conforming Services" limits, is preserved.

proposal.summary: Anchor the twelve-month lookback to the claim and make the payment carve-out cover Customer's payment obligations generally.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The cap is tied to the defined term "Fees", which is only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the mutual cap is illusory; we set it at the greater of the fees paid or payable under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000. We also confirmed that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap, and Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) remain uncapped.
